blogs.title: Meet BOFT: Orthogonal Butterfly Fine-Tuning Explained
blogs.description: An accessible tour of Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT): what it is, why orthogonal updates preserve pretrained knowledge, and how butterfly factorization slashes parameters from O(d^2) to O(d log d). Includes intuitive visuals and high-level results across LLMs, ViTs, and diffusion models.

blogs.title: LoRA vs OFT vs BOFT: Which PEFT Method Should You Pick?
blogs.description: A practitioner’s comparison of the most popular parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches. Covers when to prefer low-rank (LoRA), block-orthogonal (OFT), or butterfly-orthogonal (BOFT), with guidance on accuracy, stability, VRAM, latency, and deployment trade-offs.

blogs.title: From FFT to Fine-Tuning: A Beginner’s Guide to Butterfly Structures
blogs.description: Demystifies butterfly networks by linking the Cooley–Tukey FFT to dense information mixing in neural weights. Shows how stacking sparse orthogonal factors produces dense transformations, and why that’s a sweet spot for expressive, stable fine-tuning.

blogs.title: Hands-On: Fine-Tune a Vision Transformer, LLM, and Diffusion Model with BOFT
blogs.description: A step-by-step tutorial that adapts a ViT for new classes, a 7B LLM for domain Q&A, and a Stable Diffusion model for style control using BOFT. Includes PyTorch snippets, identity initialization, and tips for training speed, logging, and checkpoint merging with zero inference overhead.

blogs.title: Tuning the Dials: How to Choose m and b in BOFT
blogs.description: A practical guide to BOFT hyperparameters. Explains how depth (m) and block size (b) affect expressivity, parameter count, compute, and convergence. Provides rules of thumb, ablation-inspired defaults, and a decision checklist for different model sizes and tasks.

blogs.title: Stability by Design: Why Orthogonal Updates Generalize Better
blogs.description: Explains the stability advantages of orthogonal fine-tuning: preserved spectral norms, angle/geometry preservation, and smoother weight interpolation paths. Connects these properties to fewer training pathologies and better out-of-domain performance.

blogs.title: Multiplicative Dropout: Regularizing Multiplicative Adapters in BOFT
blogs.description: Introduces multiplicative dropout for BOFT, why standard dropout doesn’t fit multiplicative updates, and how selectively identity-masking butterfly blocks combats overfitting. Includes simple code patterns and guidance on p1/p2 rates.

blogs.title: Expressivity Without Bloat: What Butterfly Factorization Can Represent
blogs.description: Explores the representational power of butterfly-parameterized orthogonal matrices, when block-diagonal OFT falls short, and how kaleidoscope hierarchies extend BOFT toward full orthogonal coverage—without defaulting to full fine-tuning.

blogs.title: BOFT on the Edge: Low-VRAM and On-Device Adaptation
blogs.description: Shows how BOFT’s O(d log d) parameterization enables practical on-device fine-tuning for laptops and edge GPUs. Covers memory budgeting, mixed precision, combining with quantization (e.g., QLoRA), and merging for zero-latency inference.

blogs.title: Borrowing from Networks: The Information Transmission View of Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Translates BOFT’s core idea into a network routing mental model. Visualizes how sparse factors route information across layers to yield dense transformations, and why this perspective unlocks new structured designs beyond butterfly graphs.

blogs.title: Plugging BOFT into Hugging Face and PyTorch: An Engineering Guide
blogs.description: A developer-focused walkthrough on integrating BOFT into existing training stacks. Covers monkey-patching Linear layers, checkpoint formats, compatibility with PEFT libraries, exporting merged weights, and testing correctness and orthogonality.

blogs.title: See the Flow: Visualizing BOFT’s Butterfly Components and Interpolations
blogs.description: Presents interactive visualizations of butterfly components, sparsity patterns, and weight interpolation during training. Helps students and practitioners build intuition for how sparse factors compose into powerful dense orthogonal transforms.
